title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sets up notation for a 'polygone combinatoire'. The previous page fixed an m-gon (m ≥ 3, here intended m = 2n) in a real 2-dimensional vector space V. Its vertex set is J̃. The pair (V, J̃) is a torsor under the dihedral group D_m = μ_m ⋊ Z/2, with the standard model (C, μ_m).

On this page:
(3) D = D_J̃ = Aut(V, J̃) is the dihedral group of this particular polygon.
(4) ω = ω_J̃ = Ω(J̃) ≅ Ω(V) is the two-element set of orientations. These are orientations of the combinatorial polygon (cyclic orders on J̃ up to reversal), equivalently orientations of the real plane V.
(5) Transport of structure gives D → Aut(ω) ≅ Z/2. Its kernel is the rotation subgroup D^+, so 1 → D^+ → D → Z/2 → 1 is exact. Z/2 acts on D^+ by inversion.
(6) There is a canonical embedding ω ⊂ D^+. An orientation goes to the rotation by angle 2π/m in the positive sense of that orientation. So ω consists of the two generators of D^+ that are mutually inverse, ω' = ω^{-1}. Each choice of ω gives an isomorphism Z/mZ ≅ D^+.

Grothendieck then notes that vertices are individually labelled by R̃_i (i ∈ J̃), probably the rays or lines through the vertices. He remarks that the evenness of m has not yet been used. Evenness is equivalent to the vertex configuration being stable under the antipodal map x ↦ −x, i.e. opposite vertices exist.

The next page continues: a_0 = −1 is the unique involution in D^+. The reflections fixing vertices come in pairs r_J = r_{a_0(J)}, giving n = m/2 vertex-reflections, and there is a D-invariant Euclidean form.

Purpose: a canonical, coordinate-free 'dihedral' model of a 2n-gon. In the Teichmüller-groupoid context this is likely meant for the cyclic or dihedral structures on marked points on a real circle or boundary (cells of M_{0,n}(R), dihedral symmetry of the base points). That application is not visible on this page.
errors: No mathematical errors. Small implicit points: m ≥ 3 is needed for the two rotations in ω to be distinct, which the previous page assumes. The isomorphism Z/mZ ≅ D^+ depends on the choice of an element of ω, which is what Grothendieck says.

ideas.what: Dihedral group as automorphism group of a regular m-gon; the polygon datum is a torsor under D_m = μ_m ⋊ Z/2.
Exact sequence 1 → D^+ → D → Aut(orientations) ≅ Z/2 → 1, with Z/2 acting by inversion.
ideas.modern_name: Orientation character of the dihedral group

ideas.what: Canonical embedding of the orientation set into D^+: an orientation goes to the positive rotation by 2π/m, so the orientation torsor is identified with the pair of mutually inverse generators of D^+.
ideas.modern_name: Canonical generator of a cyclic group determined by an orientation

ideas.what: m even ⇔ vertex configuration stable under the antipodal map −1.
ideas.modern_name: Central symmetry of regular even polygons

deep.surprise_reason: Purely set-up material: a careful, canonical (torsor-style) description of the dihedral group of a regular polygon and of its orientations. This is characteristic of Grothendieck's style but contains nothing new. Whatever role it plays in the Teichmüller tower (dihedral or cyclic structures) is not visible here.
transcription_corrections: (3) reads D = D_J̃ = Aut(V, J̃). The small 'n' under J̃ looks like a stray mark or annotation rather than a subscript J̃_n.
(4): the 'V' above Ω(V) appears to be an insertion caret. Read ω = ω_J̃ = Ω(J̃) ≃ Ω(V), followed by 'ens. des orientations des poly. comb. J̃, ou de l'espace vectoriel réel V'.
'(transp. de str.)' is written under 'l'homomorphisme', i.e. the homomorphism is defined by transport of structure.
'd'angles l'une et l'autre 2π/m dans le sens de l'orientation de V': the 2π/m sits at the left margin of the next line.
Left margin: 'Z/mZ ⥲ D^+' is attached by an arrow to the sentence 'Le choix de ω ... iso correspondant'.
Last line ends 'stable par la symétrie x ↦ −x', with a crossed-out symbol before −x.
